23Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and slapped Micaiah on the cheek. “Which way did the Spirit of the LORD take from me to speak to you?” he asked. 24Micaiah replied, “You will find out on the day you go into an inner room to hide.” 25Then the king of Israel ordered, “Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon, the city governor, and to Joash, the king’s son, 26and tell them, ‘The king says this: “Put this man in prison and feed him with scant bread and scant water until I come back safely.”‘” 27Micaiah said, “If you ever come back safely, the LORD has not spoken through me.” And he added, “Listen, all you peoples!”

Ahab dies at Ramoth-gilead

28So the king of Israel went up to Ramoth-gilead, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah with him. 29The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will go into the battle in disguise, but you should put on your royal robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself, and the two of them went into the fight. 30Now the king of Aram had given an order to his chariot commanders: “Fight with no one, small or great, but the king of Israel alone.” 31When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “That is the king of Israel!” So they closed in on him to attack, and Jehoshaphat cried out. The LORD helped him; God drew them away from him. 32Once the chariot commanders saw he was not Israel’s king, they broke off the chase. 33But a man drew his bow at random and hit the king of Israel between the joints of his scale armor and the breastplate. The king said to the chariot driver, “Turn around and get me out of the battle, because I am wounded.” 34All that day the battle grew fiercer, and the king of Israel kept himself upright in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. At sunset he died.
fields.summary: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab against Aram, and the prophet Micaiah foretells defeat. Ahab dies in battle.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 19
fields.body_html:
Jehoshaphat appoints judges

1Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem. 2Jehu son of Hanani the seer came out to meet the king. He said to Jehoshaphat, “Is it right for you to help the wicked and to love those who hate the LORD? For this, wrath has come upon you from the LORD. 3Yet there is good in you, for you have rid the land of the Asherah poles and have set your heart on seeking God.” 4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but once more he went out among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim. He brought them back to the LORD, their ancestors’ God. 5He appointed judges throughout the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city. 6He said to the judges, “Think about what you are doing. You are not judging for human beings but for the LORD, and he is with you when you give a verdict. 7So now, let the fear of the LORD be upon you. Be careful in what you do, for the LORD our God does no wrong, plays no favorites and takes no bribe.” 8In Jerusalem also Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and priests and some of the heads of Israel’s families, to give judgment for the LORD and to settle disputes. And they returned to Jerusalem. 9He gave them this charge: “This is how you must act: in the fear of the LORD, faithfully, and with an undivided heart. 10Whenever a case comes to you from your fellow Israelites who live in their cities, whether it concerns bloodshed, or law and commandment, statutes and rulings, you must warn them, so that they do not incur guilt before the LORD and wrath fall on you and your fellow Israelites. Do this, and you will not incur guilt. 11Amariah the chief priest will be over you in every matter that concerns the LORD. In every matter that concerns the king, Zebadiah son of Ishmael, ruler of the house of Judah, will be over you. The Levites will serve you as officials. Act with courage, and may the LORD be with those who do good.”
fields.summary: A seer rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping Ahab. Jehoshaphat appoints judges and tells them to judge fairly.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 20
fields.body_html:
Jehoshaphat prays for help

1After this the Moabites and the Ammonites, together with some of the Meunites, came to make war on Jehoshaphat. 2Some men came and told Jehoshaphat, “A great army is coming against you from beyond the Dead Sea, from Edom. They are already at Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi.” 3Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he resolved to seek the LORD. He proclaimed a fast for all Judah. 4The people of Judah gathered to seek help from the LORD; they came from every town in Judah to seek the LORD. 5Jehoshaphat stood up in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem at the house of the LORD, in front of the new courtyard. 6He said, “LORD, God of our ancestors, are you not God in heaven? You rule over every kingdom of the nations. In your hand are power and might, and no one is able to withstand you. 7Our God, was it not you who drove out the people living in this land as your people Israel came in, and gave it for all time to the descendants of your friend Abraham? 8They have lived in it and built you a sanctuary in it for your name, saying, 9‘If disaster comes upon us, whether the sword of judgment, or disease, or famine, we will stand before this house and in your presence, since this house bears your name. We will cry out to you in our trouble, and you will hear and save us.’ 10But now look at the people of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir. You would not let Israel invade them when Israel came out of the land of Egypt, so Israel turned away from them and did not destroy them, 11and see how they repay us: they are coming to drive us out of your possession, the land you gave us to hold as our own. 12Our God, will you not judge them? We have no strength to face this great army that is coming against us. We have no idea what we should do, but our eyes are turned toward you.” 13All Judah stood before the LORD, together with their little ones, their wives and their children.

God answers and gives victory

14Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the family of Asaph, there in the middle of the assembly. 15He said, “Listen, all Judah, people of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! The LORD says this to you: ‘Do not be afraid or lose heart because of this great army, for the battle is not yours; it belongs to God. 16Tomorrow go down against them. They will be coming up by the Ascent of Ziz; you will find them where the valley ends, opposite the wilderness of Jeruel. 17You will not need to fight in this battle. Hold your ground, stand firm, and watch how the LORD will save you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or lose heart. Tomorrow go out to face them, and the LORD will be with you.’” 18Jehoshaphat bowed down with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the people of Jerusalem fell down before the LORD to worship the LORD. 19Then the Levites from the Kohathites and the Korahites stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice. 20Early in the morning they set out for the wilderness of Tekoa. As they were leaving, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Hear me, Judah and people of Jerusalem! Hold firm in your trust in the LORD your God, and you will be held firm. Trust his prophets, and you will succeed.” 21After consulting with the people, he appointed singers to sing to the LORD and to praise him in holy splendor as they went out ahead of the army, saying, “Give the LORD thanks, for his loyal love lasts forever.” 22The moment they began their shouts of joy and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the invaders from Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir who had come to attack Judah, and they were routed. 23The men of Ammon and Moab turned against the people of Mount Seir to devote them to destruction and wipe them out. When they had finished off the people of Seir, they all helped to destroy one another. 24When Judah came to the lookout point over the wilderness and looked toward the great army, there were only dead bodies lying on the ground; no one had escaped. 25When Jehoshaphat and his troops came to take the spoil, they found among them, with the dead, great quantities of goods and valuable things. They took more for themselves than they could carry. There was so much spoil that it took them three days to gather it. 26On the fourth day they gathered in the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed the LORD. That is why that place has been called the Valley of Beracah to this day. 27Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them, returned joyfully to Jerusalem, for the LORD had given them joy over their enemies. 28They came into Jerusalem with harps, lyres and trumpets, and went to the house of the LORD. 29When all the kingdoms of the lands heard that the LORD had fought against Israel’s enemies, the fear of God fell on them. 30So Jehoshaphat’s kingdom had peace, for his God gave him rest on every side.

The end of Jehoshaphat’s reign

31Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king. He reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years, and his mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. 32He followed the ways of his father Asa and did not turn aside from them, doing what was right in the sight of the LORD. 33However, the high places were not removed, and the people had still not fixed their hearts on the God of their ancestors. 34The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani, which are included in the Book of the Kings of Israel. 35Later on, Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined in an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel, a man who acted wickedly. 36He joined with him in building ships to go to Tarshish, and they built the ships at Ezion-geber. 37Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat: “Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD will break down what you have made.” And the ships were wrecked and could not sail to Tarshish.
fields.summary: A great army comes against Judah, Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast and prays, and a Levite tells the people the battle is God’s. As the singers praise, the enemies destroy one another.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 21
fields.body_html:
Jehoram king of Judah

1Then Jehoshaphat rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David. His son Jehoram became king in his place. 2He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel. 3Their father had given them many gifts of silver, gold and valuable things, together with fortified cities in Judah; the kingdom, however, he gave to Jehoram, since Jehoram was the firstborn.

4When Jehoram had taken over his father’s kingdom and made himself secure, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the officials of Israel as well. 5Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. 6He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he had married Ahab’s daughter. He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD. 7Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, for the sake of the covenant he had made with David, since he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his descendants for all time. 8During his reign Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah and set up a king of its own. 9So Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots. He rose by night and attacked the Edomites who had surrounded him and the chariot commanders. 10So Edom has been in rebellion against the rule of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled against his rule at that same time, because he had forsaken the LORD, the God of his ancestors. 11He also made high places in the hill country of Judah. He caused the people of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves and led Judah astray.

Elijah’s letter

12Then a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, which said, “The LORD the God of your ancestor David says this: Because you have not followed the ways of your father Jehoshaphat, nor the ways of Asa king of Judah, 13but have followed the way of the kings of Israel, and have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves, as the house of Ahab did, and have also killed your brothers, your own father’s family, men better than you, 14so now the LORD is going to bring a heavy blow on your people, on your sons and your wives, and on all that you own, 15and you yourself will suffer severe illness, with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day after day.” 16Then the LORD stirred up the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Cushites against Jehoram. 17They came up against Judah and broke into it. They took away as plunder all the goods they found in the king’s palace, and his sons and wives as well. Not one son was left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest. 18After all this the LORD struck him with an incurable disease of the bowels. 19In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of his disease, and he died in great pain. His people made no fire in his honor like the fire made for his ancestors. 20He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He departed with no one’s regret. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the royal tombs.
fields.summary: Jehoram kills his brothers, does evil and receives a letter of judgment from Elijah. Edom revolts, and Jehoram dies of a painful disease.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 22
fields.body_html:
Ahaziah king of Judah

1The people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram’s youngest son, king in his place, because the band of raiders who came into the camp with the Arabs had killed every one of the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.

2Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Athaliah, the granddaughter of Omri. 3He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, because his mother advised him to act wickedly. 4He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for after his father’s death they were his counselors, to his destruction. 5He also followed their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and Joram was wounded by the Arameans. 6He went back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds they had given him at Ramah, in his battle with Hazael king of Aram. Then Azariah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was wounded. 7Ahaziah’s downfall came from God, through his visit to Joram. When he arrived, he went out with Jehoram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. 8While Jehu was carrying out judgment on the house of Ahab, he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers who were attending Ahaziah, and he killed them. 9Then he searched for Ahaziah. They captured him as he was hiding in Samaria, brought him to Jehu, and put him to death. They buried him, because they said, “He is a grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.” And no one was left in the house of Ahaziah with the strength to hold the kingdom. 10Athaliah, Ahaziah’s mother, saw that her son was dead, and she set out to destroy the whole royal family of the house of Judah. 11But Jehoshabeath, the king’s daughter, took Ahaziah’s son Joash and secretly took him out from among the king’s sons who were about to be killed, and she put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, King Jehoram’s daughter and the wife of Jehoiada the priest, hid him from Athaliah, since she was Ahaziah’s sister, and Athaliah did not kill him. 12He stayed hidden with them in the house of God six years, during Athaliah’s rule over the land.
fields.summary: Ahaziah follows Ahab’s ways and is killed by Jehu. Athaliah seizes the throne, but Joash is hidden in the temple.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 23
fields.body_html:
Joash is made king

1In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage. He brought the commanders of hundreds into a covenant with him: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri. 2They went throughout Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah and the heads of families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem. 3In the house of God the whole assembly made a covenant with the king. Jehoiada said to them, “Here is the king’s son! He shall reign, as the LORD promised concerning the descendants of David. 4Here is what you must do. One third of you who come on duty on the sabbath, priests and Levites, will be gatekeepers at the doorways, 5one third will be at the king’s palace, and one third at the Foundation Gate. All the people will be in the courts of the house of the LORD. 6Let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites who minister there. They may enter, because they are holy, but all the people must keep the charge of the LORD. 7The Levites are to surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in hand. Anyone who comes into the house must be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he goes.” 8The Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest had ordered. Each brought his men, both the ones who came on duty on the sabbath and the ones who went off duty that day, for Jehoiada the priest had not released the divisions. 9Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and the two kinds of shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the house of God. 10He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in hand, from the south side of the temple to the north side, beside the altar and the temple, surrounding the king. 11Then they brought out the king’s son and put on him the crown and the testimony. They made him king, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and shouted, “Long live the king!”

Athaliah is put to death

12When Athaliah heard the noise of the people as they ran and praised the king, she went to the people at the house of the LORD. 13She looked, and there was the king, standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside him. All the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with their musical instruments were leading the praise. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, “Treason! Treason!”

14Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the troops and said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks, and anyone who follows her is to be put to death with the sword.” For the priest had said, “Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD.” 15They seized her, and when she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate at the king’s palace, they put her to death there.

Jehoiada’s reforms

16Jehoiada made a covenant binding himself, all the people and the king to be the people of the LORD. 17Then all the people went to Baal’s house and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images, and killed Mattan, Baal’s priest, before the altars. 18Jehoiada put the oversight of the house of the LORD in the hands of the Levitical priests, whom David had assigned in divisions over the house of the LORD. They were to offer the burnt offerings of the LORD as the law of Moses directs, with rejoicing and singing, as David had ordered. 19He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, to keep out anyone who was unclean in any way. 20He took with him the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers over the people and all the people of the land. He brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They went through the Upper Gate to the king’s palace and seated the king on the royal throne. 21All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was at peace. Athaliah had been put to death with the sword.
fields.summary: Jehoiada the priest crowns Joash, Athaliah is killed, and the people renew the covenant.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 24
fields.body_html:
Joash repairs the temple

1Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah from Beersheba. 2Joash did what was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest. 3Jehoiada chose two wives for him, and he became the father of sons and daughters. 4Some time later Joash set his heart on restoring the house of the LORD. 5He called the priests and the Levites together and told them, “Go out to the towns of Judah and collect money from all Israel to repair the house of your God, year by year. Do it quickly.” But the Levites did not act quickly. 6So the king summoned Jehoiada the chief priest and said to him, “Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax for the tent of the testimony, which Moses the servant of the LORD and the assembly of Israel laid down?” 7For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of God and had even used all the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals. 8At the king’s command they made a chest and placed it at the gate of the house of the LORD, on the outside. 9A proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem that the people should bring to the LORD the tax that Moses the servant of God had laid on Israel in the wilderness. 10All the officials and all the people rejoiced. They brought their money and dropped it into the chest until they had finished. 11Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king’s officials and they saw that it held a large sum of money, the king’s secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, then carry it back to its place. They did this day after day and collected a great amount of money. 12The king and Jehoiada gave the money to those in charge of the work on the house of the LORD, and they hired stonecutters and craftsmen to restore the house of the LORD. They also hired workers in iron and bronze to mend the house of the LORD. 13So the workmen did their work, and the repairs went forward under their hands. They restored the house of God to its proper design and made it strong. 14When they had finished, they brought what remained of the money to the king and Jehoiada, and with it they made articles for the house of the LORD: articles for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and other articles of gold and silver. All the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were offered continually in the house of the LORD.

15Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and he died. He was 130 years old when he died. 16He was buried among the kings in the City of David, because of the good he had done in Israel for God and for his house.

Joash turns away; Zechariah is stoned

17After Jehoiada’s death the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king, and the king listened to them. 18They forsook the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherah poles and the idols. Because of this guilt of theirs, wrath came on Judah and Jerusalem. 19Yet he sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD. The prophets warned them, but they would not listen.

20Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood up above the people and said to them, “God says this: ‘Why do you break the commandments of the LORD? You will not prosper. Because you have forsaken the LORD, he has forsaken you.’” 21But they plotted against him, and at the king’s command they stoned him to death in the courtyard of the house of the LORD. 22King Joash did not remember the faithful love that Jehoiada, Zechariah’s father, had shown him, and he killed his son. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “May the LORD see this and call you to account!”

The end of Joash’s reign

23At the turn of the year the army of Aram came up against Joash. They came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the officials of the people from among the people, and they sent all their plunder to the king of Damascus. 24Though the army of Aram came with only a few men, the LORD gave a very great army into their power, because Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their ancestors. So they carried out judgment on Joash. 25When the Arameans withdrew, they left him badly wounded. His officials conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him in his bed. So he died. He was buried in the City of David, though not in the tombs of the kings.

26These were the men who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman. 27The account of his sons, the many oracles against him, and the rebuilding of the house of God are written in the commentary on the Book of the Kings. And his son Amaziah became king in his place.
fields.summary: Joash repairs the temple, but after Jehoiada dies he turns to idols and has Zechariah the priest stoned. Aram defeats Judah, and Joash is murdered.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 25
fields.body_html:
Amaziah king of Judah

1Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan; she was from Jerusalem. 2He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not with a whole heart. 3As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his control, he executed the officials who had murdered his father the king. 4But he did not put their children to death. In this he followed the law as it stands written in the book of Moses, in which the LORD gave this command: “Parents are not to die for their children, nor children for their parents. Each one is to die only for their own sin.”

War with Edom

5Amaziah assembled the men of Judah and organized them by their ancestral families under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He mustered those twenty years old and over and found 300,000 chosen men fit for war, able to handle spear and large shield. 6He also hired 100,000 mighty warriors from Israel for about 7,500 pounds of silver. 7But a man of God came to him and said, “O king, the army of Israel must not go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with any of the people of Ephraim. 8Even if you go and fight, and are strong in battle, God will cast you down before the enemy, for God has power to help and to cast down.” 9Amaziah asked the man of God, “But what about the silver I have paid to the troops of Israel, the about 7,500 pounds?” The man of God answered, “The LORD is able to give you much more than that.” 10So Amaziah released the troops who had joined him from Ephraim and sent them home. They were furious with Judah, and they went home in a blazing rage.

11Then Amaziah took courage and led out his troops. He went to the Valley of Salt and struck down 10,000 of the people of Seir. 12The men of Judah also captured 10,000 alive. They took them up to the top of the rock and hurled them down from there, and all of them were dashed to pieces.

13Meanwhile the troops whom Amaziah had sent back, not letting them go with him into battle, raided the towns of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon. They killed 3,000 people and carried off a great deal of plunder.

Amaziah’s idols

14After Amaziah came back from defeating the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the people of Seir and set them up as his own gods. He bowed down before them and burned incense to them. 15So the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent a prophet to him, who said, “Why have you sought the gods of this people, gods that could not rescue their own people from your hand?” 16While the prophet was still speaking, the king said to him, “Have we made you the king’s counselor? Stop! Why should you be struck down?” So the prophet stopped, but he added, “I know that God has decided to destroy you, since you have done this and refused to listen to my counsel.”

Israel defeats Judah

17Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent word to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel: “Come, let us meet face to face.” 18Joash king of Israel sent back word to Amaziah king of Judah: “There was a thistle in Lebanon that sent word to a cedar in Lebanon: ‘Give your daughter to my son as his wife.’ Then a wild animal in Lebanon came by and trampled the thistle. 19You tell yourself that you have defeated Edom, and your heart has made you proud and eager for glory. Now stay at home. Why stir up trouble that will only bring you down, you and Judah with you?” 20But Amaziah would not listen, for this came from God, so that he might hand them over to their enemy, because they had sought the gods of Edom. 21So Joash king of Israel went up against him, and the two kings, he and Amaziah king of Judah, met face to face at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah. 22Judah was defeated by Israel, and every man fled to his home. 23Joash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah prisoner at Beth-shemesh; Amaziah was the son of Joash son of Jehoahaz. Then Joash brought him to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem along a stretch of about 600 feet, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate. 24He carried off all the gold and silver, and every article that was found in the house of God in the care of Obed-edom, together with the palace treasures. He also took hostages, and then he returned to Samaria.

25Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel. 26The rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 27From the time Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, some in Jerusalem formed a conspiracy against him, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish and put him to death there. 28They brought his body back on horses and buried him with his ancestors in the city of Judah.
fields.summary: Amaziah defeats Edom but brings back their gods. He challenges Israel, is defeated, and is later killed.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 26
fields.body_html:
Uzziah king of Judah

1Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, then sixteen years old, and made him king to succeed his father Amaziah. 2It was he who rebuilt Eloth and won it back for Judah, after King Amaziah had rested with his ancestors.

3Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem. 4He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done. 5He set himself to seek God during the lifetime of Zechariah, who taught him the fear of God. As long as he sought the LORD, God gave him success.

6He went out and made war on the Philistines, and broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod. Then he built towns in the region of Ashdod and elsewhere among the Philistines. 7God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and against the Meunites. 8The Ammonites brought tribute to Uzziah, and his fame reached all the way to the border of Egypt, because he had grown very strong. 9In Jerusalem Uzziah built towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate and the Angle, and he fortified them. 10He built towers in the wilderness and cut out many cisterns, for he had large herds in the Shephelah and on the plain. He had farmers and vinedressers working in the hill country and the fertile fields, for he loved the soil.

Uzziah’s army and his pride

11Uzziah had an army ready for battle, which went out to war in divisions, according to the numbers in the muster made by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the official, who worked under Hananiah, one of the king’s commanders. 12The total number of family heads over the mighty warriors was 2,600. 13Under their command was an army of 307,500 men, a powerful fighting force ready to help the king against his enemies. 14Uzziah provided the whole army with shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows and stones for slinging. 15In Jerusalem he made devices designed by skilled inventors, to be set on the towers and the corners of the walls for shooting arrows and large stones. His fame spread far and wide, for he was wonderfully helped until he became strong. 16But when he had become strong, his heart grew proud, to his own ruin. He was unfaithful to the LORD his God, and he went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the incense altar. 17Azariah the priest went in after him, along with eighty priests of the LORD, men of courage. 18They confronted King Uzziah and said to him, “It is not your place, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD. That belongs to the priests, the sons of Aaron, who have been set apart to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful, and this will bring you no honor from the LORD God.” 19Uzziah became furious. He had a censer in his hand ready to burn incense, and while he raged at the priests, a serious skin disease broke out on his forehead, there in front of the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense. 20When Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, there on his forehead was the skin disease! They rushed him out of there, and he himself hurried to leave, because the LORD had struck him. 21King Uzziah had a serious skin disease until the day he died. He lived in a separate house because of the disease, for he was shut out of the house of the LORD, while his son Jotham was in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land. 22The rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, were written down by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. 23Then Uzziah rested with his ancestors, and they buried him near his ancestors in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, “He has a serious skin disease.” His son Jotham became king in his place.
fields.summary: Uzziah prospers while he seeks God, but in his pride he burns incense in the temple and is struck with skin disease.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 27
fields.body_html:
Jotham king of Judah

1Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok. 2He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done, except that he did not go into the temple of the LORD. But the people still behaved corruptly. 3He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and he did much building on the wall of Ophel. 4In the hill country of Judah he built cities, and in the wooded areas he put up fortresses and towers. 5He fought against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. That year the Ammonites gave him about 7,500 pounds of silver, about 60,000 bushels of wheat and about 60,000 bushels of barley. The Ammonites paid him the same in the second and third years as well. 6Jotham grew strong, because he kept his ways steady before the LORD his God. 7The rest of the acts of Jotham, with all his wars and his ways, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. 8He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. 9Then Jotham rested with his ancestors, and they buried him in the City of David. His son Ahaz became king in his place.
fields.summary: Jotham grows strong because he walks steadily before God.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 28
fields.body_html:
Ahaz king of Judah

1Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the sight of the LORD, as his ancestor David had done. 2He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel; he also made images of cast metal for the Baals. 3He burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom and burned his sons in the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations that the LORD had driven out ahead of the Israelites. 4He offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places, on the hills and under every leafy tree. 5So the LORD his God handed him over to the king of Aram. The Arameans defeated him, took a great many of his people captive and brought them to Damascus. He was also handed over to the king of Israel, who struck him a heavy blow.

6In one day Pekah son of Remaliah killed 120,000 in Judah, all of them valiant men, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their ancestors. 7Zichri, an Ephraimite warrior, killed Maaseiah the king’s son, Azrikam the officer in charge of the palace, and Elkanah, who was second to the king.

8The Israelites took 200,000 of their own relatives captive, women, sons and daughters. They also seized a great deal of plunder from them and brought the plunder to Samaria.

Oded and the captives from Judah

9But a prophet of the LORD named Oded was there. He went out to meet the army as it came to Samaria and said to them, “Look, it was because the LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah that he handed them over to you. But you have slaughtered them in a rage that has reached up to heaven. 10And now you intend to force the people of Judah and Jerusalem to become your male and female slaves. But are you not yourselves guilty of wrongs against the LORD your God? 11Now listen to me: send back the captives you have taken from your own relatives, for the fierce anger of the LORD is upon you.”

12Then some of the chiefs of the Ephraimites, Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum and Amasa son of Hadlai, stood up to confront those returning from the war. 13They said to them, “You must not bring the captives here. What you intend would bring guilt on us before the LORD and add to our sins and our guilt. Our guilt is already great, and fierce anger is upon Israel.”

14So the armed men left the captives and the plunder in the presence of the officials and the whole assembly. 15Then the men who had been named for the task got up and took charge of the captives. From the plunder they clothed all among them who were naked. They gave them clothes and sandals, food and drink, and anointed them with oil. They put all who were too weak to walk on donkeys and brought them to their relatives at Jericho, the city of palm trees. Then they went back to Samaria.

Ahaz turns to Assyria

16At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help. 17The Edomites had come again, attacked Judah and carried off captives. 18The Philistines had raided the towns of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah. They captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon and Gederoth, as well as Soco, Timnah and Gimzo with their villages, and they settled there. 19The LORD brought Judah low on account of Ahaz king of Israel, because he had let Judah throw off all restraint and had been grossly unfaithful to the LORD. 20Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came against him and brought him distress instead of strength. 21Ahaz took a share of the wealth of the house of the LORD, of the royal palace and of the officials, and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did him no good. 22In his time of distress this same King Ahaz became even more unfaithful to the LORD. 23He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him, and said, “Since the gods of the kings of Aram help them, I will sacrifice to them so that they will help me.” But they brought ruin on him and on all Israel. 24Ahaz collected the vessels of the house of God and cut them in pieces. He shut the doors of the house of the LORD and made himself altars on every street corner in Jerusalem. 25In each and every town of Judah he set up high places for burning incense to other gods, and he provoked the LORD, the God of his ancestors, to anger. 26The rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 27Then Ahaz rested with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem; but they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. His son Hezekiah became king in his place.
fields.summary: Ahaz worships other gods and is defeated by Aram and Israel. A prophet persuades Israel to free the captives from Judah, and Ahaz closes the temple.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 29
fields.body_html:
Hezekiah cleanses the temple

1Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah. 2He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, in every way as his ancestor David had done. 3In his first year as king, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and made them strong again. 4He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the open square on the east side. 5He said to them, “Listen to me, you Levites! Consecrate yourselves now. Then consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors, and carry everything impure out of the holy place. 6Our fathers were unfaithful and did what was evil in the sight of the LORD our God. They forsook him; they turned their faces from the place where the LORD dwells and showed it their backs. 7They even shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps. They did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel. 8So the wrath of the LORD came upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them an object of terror, horror and hissing, as you can see with your own eyes. 9Because of this our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, our daughters and our wives are in captivity. 10I have now set my heart on making a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, in the hope that the heat of his anger will turn away from us. 11My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him and serve him, to be his ministers and to burn incense.”

12Then the Levites set to work: from the descendants of the Kohathites, Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah; from the descendants of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; from the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah, 13from the descendants of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; from the descendants of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah,

14from the descendants of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and from the descendants of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel. 15They gathered their relatives and consecrated themselves, and they came to cleanse the house of the LORD, as the king had commanded by the words of the LORD. 16The priests entered the inner part of the LORD’s house to cleanse it. Everything unclean that they found in the temple of the LORD they brought out into the court of the LORD’s house, and the Levites took it from them and carried it outside to the Kidron Valley. 17The consecration began on the first day of the first month, and by the eighth day of the month they had come as far as the porch of the LORD. Then for eight days they consecrated the house of the LORD, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

18Then they went in to King Hezekiah and said, “We have cleansed the whole house of the LORD: the altar of burnt offering together with all its utensils, and the table for the rows of bread together with all its utensils, 19and all the utensils that King Ahaz discarded during his reign, when he was unfaithful, we have prepared and consecrated. They are there in front of the altar of the LORD.”

Temple worship restored

20King Hezekiah rose early and gathered the officials of the city, and he went up to the LORD’s house. 21Seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats were brought as a sin offering on behalf of the kingdom, the sanctuary and Judah. The king told the priests, Aaron’s descendants, to offer them up on the LORD’s altar. 22So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and splashed it against the altar. Next they slaughtered the rams and splashed their blood against the altar, and then they slaughtered the lambs and splashed their blood against the altar. 23Then the goats for the sin offering were brought before the king and the assembly, and these laid their hands on them. 24The priests slaughtered the goats and applied their blood to the altar as a sin offering, making atonement for all Israel. The king had said that the burnt offering and the sin offering were to be for all Israel. 25He placed the Levites in the LORD’s house with cymbals, harps and lyres, as David had commanded, together with Gad the king’s seer and Nathan the prophet. The command had come from the LORD through his prophets.

26The Levites stood ready with David’s instruments, and the priests with the trumpets.

27Then Hezekiah ordered the burnt offering to be offered on the altar. When the burnt offering began, the song to the LORD began too, with the trumpets, accompanied by the instruments of David king of Israel. 28The whole assembly bowed down in worship while the singers sang and the trumpeters sounded the trumpets. All this went on until the burnt offering was finished. 29When the offering was finished, the king and everyone present with him knelt down and worshiped. 30King Hezekiah and the officials told the Levites to praise the LORD using the words of David and of Asaph the seer. They praised joyfully, and they bowed their heads and worshiped.

31Then Hezekiah said, “Now you have dedicated yourselves to the LORD. Come near; bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the LORD’s house.” The assembly brought their sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who were willing at heart brought burnt offerings. 32The number of burnt offerings that the assembly brought was seventy bulls, 100 rams and 200 lambs. All these were for burnt offerings to the LORD. 33The consecrated offerings were 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep. 34But the priests were too few to skin all the burnt offerings. So their relatives the Levites helped them until the task was done and the priests had consecrated themselves, for the Levites were more upright in heart to consecrate themselves than the priests. 35Burnt offerings were also plentiful, together with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings that went with each burnt offering. In this way the service of the LORD’s house was set in order. 36Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced over what God had prepared for the people, for the thing had come about suddenly.
fields.summary: Hezekiah opens and cleanses the temple, and the priests and Levites restore its worship with sacrifices and songs.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 30
fields.body_html:
Hezekiah calls Israel to the Passover

1Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters as well to Ephraim and Manasseh, calling them to come to Jerusalem, to the house of the LORD, to keep the Passover for the LORD, the God of Israel. 2The king, his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem decided to keep the Passover in the second month. 3They had not been able to keep it at the usual time, because too few priests had consecrated themselves and the people had not yet gathered in Jerusalem. 4The plan seemed right to the king and to the whole assembly. 5So they issued a decree to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that the people should come to Jerusalem to keep the Passover for the LORD, the God of Israel. For they had not kept it in great numbers, as it is written. 6The couriers went throughout all Israel and Judah with the letters from the king and his officials. As the king had commanded, they said, “Israelites, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, and he will return to those of you who are left, who escaped from the grasp of the kings of Assyria. 7Do not be like your ancestors and your relatives, who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their ancestors, so that he made them an object of horror, as you see for yourselves. 8Now do not stiffen your necks as your ancestors did. Give yourselves to the LORD and come to his sanctuary, which he has made holy forever. Serve the LORD your God, so that his burning anger may turn away from you. 9For if you return to the LORD, your relatives and your children will be shown compassion by those who took them captive, and they will come back to this land. The LORD your God is gracious and compassionate, and he will not turn his face away from you if you turn back to him.”

10The couriers passed from town to town in the land of Ephraim and Manasseh and on as far as Zebulun, but people laughed at them and mocked them. 11Yet some people from Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem. 12In Judah too the hand of God was at work, giving them one heart to carry out the command of the king and the officials, which followed the word of the LORD. 13A great crowd gathered in Jerusalem to keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread in the second month, a very large assembly. 14They set to work and removed the altars in Jerusalem. They also removed all the incense altars and threw them into the Kidron Valley. 15They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. Ashamed, the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of the LORD. 16They took their usual places as the law of Moses the man of God prescribes, and the priests splashed the blood that they received from the Levites. 17Since many in the assembly had not consecrated themselves, the Levites took charge of slaughtering the Passover lambs for all who were not clean, to consecrate them to the LORD. 18A large part of the people, many of them from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, had not purified themselves, and yet they ate the Passover in a way that did not keep to what is written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, “May the LORD, who is good, pardon 19everyone who sets their heart on seeking God, the LORD, the God of their ancestors, even if they are not clean as the sanctuary requires.”

20The LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

The festival kept for fourteen days

21The Israelites who were present in Jerusalem kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy, while the Levites and the priests praised the LORD day after day, playing loud instruments for the LORD.

22Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good skill in the service of the LORD. For the seven days of the festival they ate the festival meals, offering peace offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

23Then the whole assembly decided to keep the festival for another seven days, and they kept seven more days with joy. 24Hezekiah king of Judah provided 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep for the assembly, and the officials provided 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep. A great number of priests consecrated themselves. 25The whole assembly of Judah rejoiced, together with the priests and the Levites, the whole assembly that had come from Israel, and the outsiders who had come from the land of Israel or who lived in Judah. 26So there was great joy in Jerusalem, because nothing like this had happened in Jerusalem since the time of Solomon son of David, king of Israel.

27Then the Levitical priests stood and blessed the people. Their voice was heard, and their prayer reached heaven, his holy dwelling place.
fields.summary: Hezekiah invites all Israel and Judah to keep the Passover in Jerusalem, and there is great joy, the greatest since Solomon’s day.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 31
fields.body_html:
Contributions for the priests and Levites

1When all this was over, all Israel who were there went out to the towns of Judah. They smashed the standing stones, cut down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and the altars throughout Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh as well, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the Israelites went back to their own towns, each to his own property.

2Hezekiah set the priests and the Levites in their divisions, each man according to his service, both priests and Levites, for burnt offerings and peace offerings, to minister and to give thanks and praise in the gates of the camps of the LORD.

3The king’s share from his own possessions went for the burnt offerings: those offered morning and evening, and those for the Sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed festivals, as it is written in the law of the LORD. 4He also told the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the priests and the Levites their share, so that they could give themselves fully to the law of the LORD. 5As soon as the order went out, the Israelites gave generously of the firstfruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey and all the produce of the fields. They brought in a great amount, a tithe of everything. 6The Israelites and the people of Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought a tithe of cattle and sheep, and a tithe of the holy things that had been consecrated to the LORD their God, and they piled them up in heap after heap.

7They began making the heaps in the third month and finished in the seventh month.

8When Hezekiah and the officials came and looked at the heaps, they blessed the LORD and his people Israel.

9Hezekiah asked the priests and the Levites about the heaps. 10Azariah the chief priest, of the family of Zadok, answered him, “Since the people began to bring the contributions into the house of the LORD, we have eaten our fill, with plenty left over, for the LORD has blessed his people. This great amount is what is left.”

Storerooms and their overseers

11Then Hezekiah gave orders to prepare storerooms in the house of the LORD, and they prepared them. 12They faithfully brought in the contributions, the tithes and the holy gifts. Conaniah the Levite was the chief officer over them, with his brother Shimei next in rank. 13Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath and Benaiah were overseers under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, appointed by King Hezekiah and by Azariah the chief officer of the house of God. 14Kore son of Imnah the Levite, keeper of the East Gate, had charge of the freewill offerings made to God, to give out the contributions for the LORD and the most holy gifts. 15Under him, in the towns of the priests, were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah and Shecaniah, who faithfully gave out portions to their fellow priests and Levites by their divisions, to the great and the small alike, 16apart from the males three years old and up who were enrolled in the genealogies, all who came into the house of the LORD to do the work each day required, serving in their duties by their divisions. 17The priests were enrolled by their ancestral families, and the Levites from twenty years old and up by their duties and their divisions, 18and to all who were enrolled with them: their little children, their wives, their sons and their daughters, the whole company. For they had been faithful in keeping themselves holy. 19For the descendants of Aaron, the priests, who lived in the pasturelands around their towns, there were men in every town who were named to give portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled among the Levites. 20Hezekiah did this throughout Judah. He did what was good and right and faithful before the LORD his God. 21Every work he took up in the service of the house of God, and in keeping the law and the commandments, he did with all his heart, seeking his God; and he prospered.
fields.summary: The people destroy idols throughout the land, and Hezekiah organizes the priests and Levites and their support.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 32
fields.body_html:
Sennacherib threatens Jerusalem

1After these faithful deeds, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah. He camped against the fortified cities, intending to break into them and take them for himself. 2When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and was set on making war against Jerusalem, 3he consulted with his officials and his warriors about stopping the water of the springs outside the city, and they supported him. 4A great many people gathered and blocked all the springs and the stream running across the land. “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find water in plenty?” they said. 5Hezekiah took courage. He rebuilt all the wall where it was broken down and raised it up to the towers, and he built another wall outside it. He strengthened the Millo in the City of David and made large numbers of weapons and shields. 6He appointed military commanders over the people and gathered them to him in the square at the city gate. Then he spoke encouragement to them: 7“Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or discouraged because of the king of Assyria and all the horde that is with him, for there is more on our side than on his. 8With him is only an arm of flesh, but we have the LORD our God with us, to help us and fight our battles for us.” And the people took confidence from the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

9After this, while Sennacherib king of Assyria was at Lachish with all his forces, he sent his officials to Jerusalem, to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all the people of Judah who were in Jerusalem, with this message: 10“Sennacherib king of Assyria says this: What are you relying on, that you stay in Jerusalem under siege? 11Is Hezekiah not misleading you, handing you over to die of hunger and thirst, when he says, ‘The LORD our God will rescue us from the power of the king of Assyria’? 12Did this same Hezekiah not get rid of his high places and his altars and tell Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must bow down before one altar and burn your offerings on it’? 13Do you not know what I and my forefathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of the nations in those lands ever able to rescue their land from my hand? 14Which of all the gods of these nations that my forefathers devoted to destruction was able to rescue its people from my hand? How then could your God rescue you from my hand? 15So now, do not let Hezekiah fool you or mislead you like this. Do not believe him. No god of any nation or kingdom has been able to rescue its people from my hand or from the hand of my forefathers. How much less will your God rescue you from my hand!” 16His officials said still more against the LORD God and against his servant Hezekiah. 17He also wrote letters to insult the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against him: “Just as the gods of the nations of other lands have not rescued their people from my hand, so Hezekiah’s God will not rescue his people from my hand.” 18They shouted in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem on the wall, trying to frighten and terrify them so that they could take the city. 19They spoke about the God of Jerusalem as if he were one of the gods of the earth’s peoples, the work of human hands.

The LORD saves Jerusalem

20Then King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz prayed about this and cried out to heaven.

21The LORD sent an angel, who cut off every mighty warrior, ruler and commander in the Assyrian king’s camp. Sennacherib went back to his own land in disgrace. And when he went into the house of his god, some of his own offspring cut him down there with the sword. 22In this way the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the power of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the power of everyone else, and he took care of them on every side. 23Many brought gifts to the LORD in Jerusalem and costly presents to Hezekiah king of Judah, and from then on he was highly regarded by all the nations.

Hezekiah’s illness, pride and death

24In those days Hezekiah fell ill and was close to death. He prayed to the LORD, who answered him and gave him a sign. 25But Hezekiah did not respond in keeping with the kindness shown to him, because his heart became proud. So wrath came on him and on Judah and Jerusalem. 26Then Hezekiah humbled himself for his proud heart, he and the people of Jerusalem with him, so the wrath of the LORD did not come on them in Hezekiah’s days. 27Hezekiah had very great wealth and honor. He made himself treasuries for silver and gold, for precious stones and spices, for shields and for all kinds of valuable things, 28and storehouses for the harvest of grain, new wine and oil. He also made stalls for every kind of livestock and folds for the flocks. 29He also built towns for himself and acquired great numbers of flocks and herds, for God had given him very great wealth. 30It was Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and channeled them straight down to the west side of the City of David. Hezekiah succeeded in everything he did. 31And so, in the matter of the envoys of the officials of Babylon who were sent to him to ask about the sign that had happened in the land, God left him to himself to test him, to know everything that was in his heart. 32The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his faithful deeds are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 33Then Hezekiah rested with his ancestors, and they buried him on the ascent to the tombs of David’s descendants. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him at his death. His son Manasseh became king in his place.
fields.summary: Sennacherib of Assyria invades, and Hezekiah encourages the people to trust God. An angel destroys the Assyrian army, and Hezekiah’s illness and pride are recorded.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 33
fields.body_html:
Manasseh king of Judah

1Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. 2He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, following the detestable practices of the nations that the LORD had driven out ahead of the Israelites. 3He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had pulled down. He set up altars for the Baals and made Asherah poles. He bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them. 4He built altars in the house of the LORD, the house about which the LORD had said, “My name will be in Jerusalem forever.” 5He built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD. 6He made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, practiced fortune-telling, read omens and practiced sorcery, and consulted a medium and a spiritist. He did much evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking him to anger. 7He placed the carved idol he had made in the house of God, about which God had said to David and to his son Solomon, “In this house, and in Jerusalem, the city I chose from among all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever. 8And I will not again make the feet of Israel leave the land I assigned to your ancestors, if only they will be careful to do all that I have commanded them, the whole law, the statutes and the rulings given through Moses.” 9Manasseh led Judah and the people of Jerusalem astray, so that they did more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed ahead of the Israelites.

Manasseh’s captivity and return

10The LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they paid no attention. 11So the LORD brought against them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, who captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze chains and took him to Babylon. 12In his distress he sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself deeply before the God of his ancestors. 13He prayed to him, and he was moved by his prayer. He heard his plea for mercy and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God. 14After this he built an outer wall for the City of David, west of Gihon in the valley, as far as the entrance at the Fish Gate. He carried it around the Ophel and made it very high. He also stationed army commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah. 15He removed the foreign gods from the house of the LORD, and the idol as well, together with every altar he had built on the temple mount and elsewhere in Jerusalem, and threw them outside the city. 16He restored the altar of the LORD and offered on it peace offerings and thank offerings, and he commanded Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel. 17Even so, the people still sacrificed at the high places, though only to the LORD their God. 18The rest of the acts of Manasseh, including the prayer he made to his God and what the seers said to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are found in the Records of the Kings of Israel. 19His prayer and how God answered his plea, every sin and act of unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and erected Asherah poles and carved idols before he humbled himself, are written in the records of Hozai. 20Then Manasseh rested with his ancestors, and they buried him at his palace. His son Amon became king in his place.

Amon king of Judah

21Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. 22He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done, offering sacrifices to all the carved idols his father had made and serving them. 23Unlike his father Manasseh, he did not humble himself before the LORD. Instead Amon added more and more to his guilt. 24His officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace. 25Then the people of the land killed all who had plotted against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
fields.summary: Manasseh does great evil, is taken captive to Babylon, humbles himself and is restored. Amon reigns briefly and is murdered.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 34
fields.body_html:
Josiah’s reforms

1Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. 2He did what was right in the sight of the LORD and walked in the ways of his ancestor David. He did not turn aside to the right or to the left. 3In his eighth year as king, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David. In the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem, clearing away the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved images and the cast images. 4Under his direction they tore down the altars of the Baals, and he cut down the incense altars that stood above them. He smashed the Asherah poles, the carved images and the cast images, crushed them to dust, and scattered the dust over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them. 5He burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and so he purged Judah and Jerusalem. 6In the towns of Manasseh, Ephraim and Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, in their ruins all around, 7he tore down the altars and the Asherah poles, crushed the carved images to dust, and cut down all the incense altars in every part of the land of Israel. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

The book of the law is found

8When he had purged the land and the house, in the eighteenth year of his reign, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the city governor and Joah son of Joahaz, the recorder, to make repairs on the house of the LORD his God. 9They came to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the money brought into the house of God, which the Levites who kept the doors had collected from Manasseh and Ephraim, from all the rest of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin, and they returned to Jerusalem. 10They handed it to the men doing the work, who had been put in charge of the house of the LORD, and they paid it to the workmen in the house of the LORD to mend and repair the house. 11They gave it to the craftsmen and the builders to buy dressed stone, and timber for the braces and for the beams of the buildings that the kings of Judah had allowed to fall into ruin. 12The men did the work honestly. Over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the descendants of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the descendants of Kohath, to direct the work. And the Levites, all who were skilled with musical instruments, 13were over the porters and directed all the workmen in every kind of task. Some of the Levites were scribes, officials and gatekeepers. 14As they were taking out the money brought into the house of the LORD, the priest Hilkiah found the book of the law of the LORD, given through Moses. 15Hilkiah spoke up and said to Shaphan the secretary, “In the house of the LORD I have found the book of the law.” Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan. 16Shaphan took the book to the king and also reported to him: “Your officials are doing everything that was entrusted to them. 17They have emptied out the money found in the house of the LORD and handed it over to the overseers and to the men doing the work.” 18Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, “Hilkiah the priest has handed me a book.” And Shaphan read from it aloud to the king. 19When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes. 20Then the king gave orders to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary and Asaiah the king’s official, 21“Go and ask the LORD on my behalf, and on behalf of those who are left in Israel and in Judah, about the words of the book that has been found. Great is the LORD’s anger that has been poured out on us, because our ancestors did not keep the word of the LORD or do all that is written in this book.”

22So Hilkiah and those the king had sent went to the prophet Huldah, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. Her home was in the Second Quarter of Jerusalem, and they spoke with her about this.

23She said to them, “The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: Tell the man who sent you to me,

24‘The LORD says this: I am about to bring disaster on this place and on those who live in it, all the curses written in the book that was read before the king of Judah, 25because they have abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, provoking me to anger with all the works of their hands. So my wrath will pour out on this place, and it will not be put out.’ 26But to the king of Judah, who sent you to ask the LORD, say this: ‘The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: As for the words you have heard, 27because your heart was tender, and when you heard his words against this place and its people you humbled yourself before God; and because you humbled yourself before me, tore your clothes and wept before me, I in turn have heard you, declares the LORD. 28I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. You will not see with your own eyes all the disaster I am going to bring on this place and on those who live in it.’” Then they took her answer back to the king.

Josiah renews the covenant

29Then the king sent word and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem. 30The king went up to the house of the LORD, and with him went all the people of Judah and those who lived in Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites, and all the people, from the greatest to the least. In their hearing he read out all the words of the book of the covenant, which had been found in the house of the LORD. 31The king stood in his place and made the covenant in the presence of the LORD: to follow the LORD and to keep his commandments, his decrees and his statutes with all his heart and all his being, and so to carry out the words of the covenant written in this book. 32He had everyone who was present in Jerusalem and Benjamin commit themselves to it, and the people of Jerusalem acted in keeping with the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors. 33Josiah removed all the detestable things from all the lands that belonged to the Israelites, and he made everyone present in Israel serve the LORD their God. As long as he lived, they did not turn away from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
fields.summary: Josiah seeks God, removes idols, and repairs the temple, where the book of the law is found. Huldah the prophet speaks of judgment, and Josiah renews the covenant.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 35
fields.body_html:
Josiah keeps the Passover

1Josiah kept a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem. They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month. 2He put the priests at their posts and urged them on in the service of the house of the LORD. 3He said to the Levites, who taught all Israel and who were holy to the LORD, “Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built. You do not need to carry it on your shoulders. Serve the LORD your God now, and serve his people Israel. 4Get yourselves ready by your families, in your divisions, following the written orders of David king of Israel and of his son Solomon. 5Take your stand in the holy place, family division by family division of your fellow Israelites, the lay people, with a section of a Levite family for each. 6Slaughter the Passover lamb, consecrate yourselves, and prepare it for your fellow Israelites, so as to do what the LORD said through Moses.”

7Josiah gave the lay people animals from the flock, lambs and young goats, all for the Passover offerings for everyone who was there, 30,000 in number, and 3,000 cattle. These came from the king’s own property.

8His officials also gave freely to the people, the priests and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, the chief officers of the house of God, gave 2,600 Passover offerings and 300 cattle to the priests. 9Conaniah, with his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, gave the Levites 5,000 Passover offerings and 500 cattle. 10So the service was made ready. The priests took their places, and the Levites stood by their divisions, as the king had commanded. 11They slaughtered the Passover lambs, and the priests splashed the blood they received from the Levites, while the Levites skinned the animals. 12They set aside the burnt offerings to give them to the divisions of the families of the lay people, to offer to the LORD, following what is written in the book of Moses. The cattle were handled in the same way. 13They roasted the Passover lambs over the fire according to the rule, and they boiled the holy offerings in pots, kettles and pans and quickly brought them to all the lay people. 14Afterward they prepared it for themselves and the priests, since the priests, the sons of Aaron, were kept busy offering the burnt offerings and the fat until nightfall. So the Levites prepared it for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron. 15The singers, the sons of Asaph, were in their places, as David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king’s seer had commanded. The gatekeepers stood at each gate. They did not have to leave their posts, because their fellow Levites prepared the Passover for them. 16So all the service of the LORD was made ready that day, for keeping the Passover and for burnt offerings to be offered on the altar of the LORD, by King Josiah’s command. 17The Israelites who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days. 18No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. Not one of the kings of Israel had kept such a Passover as Josiah kept with the priests and the Levites, with all Judah and the Israelites who were there, and with the people of Jerusalem.

19This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign. 20After all this, when Josiah had put the temple in order, Neco king of Egypt came up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates River, and Josiah marched out to meet him. 21But Neco sent messengers to him to say, “What have I to do with you, king of Judah? I am not coming against you today, but against the house with which I am at war, and God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, for your own sake, so that he does not destroy you.” 22But Josiah would not turn away from him. Instead he disguised himself to fight him. He did not listen to Neco’s words, which came from the mouth of God, and he went to fight in the plain of Megiddo. 23Archers shot at King Josiah, and he said to his officials, “Take me away, because I am badly wounded.” 24So his officials lifted him out of the chariot, set him in the second chariot he had, and took him to Jerusalem. There he died, and he was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

25Jeremiah sang a lament for Josiah, and all the singing men and women speak of Josiah in their laments to this day. They made them a custom in Israel, and they are written in the Laments. 26The rest of the acts of Josiah, and his faithful deeds in keeping with what is written in the law of the LORD, 27and his acts, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
fields.summary: Josiah keeps a great Passover. He opposes Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo and is killed, and all Judah mourns him.

fields.title: 2 Chronicles 36
fields.body_html:
The last kings of Judah

1The people of the land then took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in Jerusalem to succeed his father. 2Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. 3The king of Egypt removed him from the throne in Jerusalem and imposed on the land a payment of about 7,500 pounds of silver and about 75 pounds of gold. 4The king of Egypt made Eliakim, the brother of Jehoahaz, king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed Eliakim’s name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took Jehoahaz, Eliakim’s brother, and brought him to Egypt.

5Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD his God. 6Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and put him in bronze chains to take him off to Babylon. 7Nebuchadnezzar also carried off to Babylon some of the vessels from the house of the LORD and placed them in his temple there. 8The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, the detestable things he did and what was found against him, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin became king in his place.

9Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD. 10In the spring of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and brought him to Babylon, along with the precious vessels of the house of the LORD. He made Jehoiachin’s relative Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem.

The fall of Jerusalem

11Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. 12He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke the word that came from the LORD. 13He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear an oath by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart, and would not turn to the LORD, the God of Israel. 14In the same way all the leaders of the priests and the people were more and more unfaithful, following all the detestable practices of the nations, and they defiled the house of the LORD that he had set apart as holy in Jerusalem. 15The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them through his messengers again and again, because he felt compassion for his people and for his dwelling place. 16But they made fun of God’s messengers, scorned his words and sneered at his prophets, until the fury of the LORD rose up against his people and nothing could heal them. 17So he brought the king of the Chaldeans against them, and the king put their young men to the sword in their own sanctuary. He had no compassion on young man or young woman, on the old or the frail.
